outcome: Proved: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth posted a claimed complete proof for all finite groups and all primes on arXiv on 27 Oct 2024 (v2 1 May 2025); it was accepted by Annals of Mathematics on 17 Apr 2025 and published in vol. 203 (2026), pp. 933-1032. The sources I read name no AI system in the proof, and I found no erratum, refutation or retraction of it.
problem_asks: (1) For every finite group G: the number of complex irreducible characters of G whose degree is not divisible by a prime p equals the number of complex irreducible characters of the normalizer N_G(P) whose degree is not divisible by p, where P is a Sylow p-subgroup of G. (2) This holds for every prime p (a universal claim over primes). (3) P may be any Sylow p-subgroup; the count does not depend on the choice because Sylow subgroups are conjugate, so this is wording rather than extra content. Reading note: the Wikipedia wording leaves implicit that the normalizer count is also restricted to p'-degree characters; the standard statement has that restriction and I have read it that way.

events.what_happened: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth, 'The McKay Conjecture on character degrees' (arXiv:2410.20392), claims a full proof: for every prime l and every finite group, the number of irreducible complex characters of degree prime to l equals that of the normalizer of a Sylow l-subgroup (the paper's Theorem A, labelled (MK)). The proof uses the Isaacs-Malle-Navarro (2007) reduction to the inductive McKay condition for finite simple groups, then verifies that condition using the classification of finite simple groups; the main technical work concerns characters of normalizers of Sylow d-tori (d >= 3) in simply connected groups of type D_l. The result was announced to audiences from October 2023 (Quanta says to more than 100 mathematicians; Wikipedia says 'in various conferences'), but the first public written argument is the arXiv v1 posted 27 Oct 2024. It was received by Annals of Mathematics on 31 Jul 2024, revised 13 Apr 2025, accepted 17 Apr 2025, and published in Annals 203(3), 2026, pp. 933-1032.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 27 Oct 2024; v2 1 May 2025 (current arXiv version). Journal: Annals of Mathematics 203(3), 2026, pp. 933-1032; received 2024-07-31, revised 2025-04-13, accepted 2025-04-17 (Annals page; the page gives no publication day). The Oct 2023 talks are not dated here: per section 5.1 the first written argument is the arXiv posting.
events.delivers: Settles the whole conjecture as stated: for every finite group X and every prime l, |Irr_l'(X)| = |Irr_l'(N_X(S))| for a Sylow l-subgroup S (arXiv HTML, Theorem A). The paper states the result without restriction to a class of groups or to particular primes. Its proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups, which the abstract names as an input.
events.remains: None of problem_asks is left open by the paper's own statements. The only wording gap is the one noted in problem_asks (the normalizer count's p'-restriction is implicit in the Wikipedia text and explicit in the paper).

events.time_since_posted: About 2 years at 13 Oct 2026 (v1 27 Oct 2024). I found no written expert digest, blog working through the proof, MathOverflow thread, zbMATH or MathSciNet review, or erratum in searches; the only public engagement found is the praise above and later papers that cite it.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture as stated: the equality holds for every finite group and every prime.

events.what_happened: I. M. Isaacs, Gunter Malle and Gabriel Navarro, 'A reduction theorem for the McKay conjecture', Invent. Math. 170(1) (2007), 33-101, DOI 10.1007/S00222-007-0057-Y. It reduces the McKay conjecture for all finite groups to an 'inductive McKay condition' on finite simple groups. The reduction is described in the Cabanes-Späth and Giannelli arXiv texts (both opened), and the journal record was opened for metadata only.
events.delivers: A reduction only: McKay for all finite groups follows once the inductive McKay condition holds for every finite simple group. It proves no instance of the conjecture by itself.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks; the inductive condition on simple groups is what the 2024 proof verifies.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in Invent. Math. 170 (2007). Referee reports not public.
checked_by.where: https://doi.org/10.1007/S00222-007-0057-Y (metadata only; the Springer page redirected to a login)

events.direction: Reduces the conjecture to a condition on simple groups; does not confirm or refute the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Gunter Malle and Britta Späth, 'Characters of odd degree' (arXiv:1506.07690, 25 Jun 2015), prove the McKay conjecture for the prime 2 for all finite groups, via the inductive McKay condition for groups of Lie type at primes whose Sylow subgroup sits in a maximally split torus, and the fact that odd-degree characters lie in the principal Harish-Chandra series. Published in Annals of Mathematics 184(3) (2016), 869-908 (from the search listing; not opened).
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (25 Jun 2015). Annals 184(3), 2016, pp. 869-908.
events.delivers: A restricted case: McKay for p = 2 for all finite groups (equivalently, for characters of odd degree).
events.remains: The conjecture for every odd prime p. This event was overtaken by the 2024 proof for all primes.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2016 after refereeing (journal listing seen in search; not opened).

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for p = 2.

events.what_happened: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth, 'Inductive McKay condition for finite simple groups of type C' (arXiv:1612.03741, 12 Dec 2016). Verifies the inductive McKay condition for finite projective symplectic groups, a step in the Isaacs-Malle-Navarro reduction.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 12 Dec 2016 (version history beyond v1 not read).
events.delivers: Verifies one family of simple groups for the inductive McKay condition (type C). This is a step in the reduction, not a case of the McKay statement.
events.remains: The McKay conjecture for all finite groups; the inductive condition for the other families of simple groups.
events.direction: Partial verification of a condition that, with the reduction, implies McKay; does not decide the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth, 'Descent equalities and the inductive McKay condition for types B and E' (arXiv:1903.11667, 27 Mar 2019). Verifies the inductive McKay condition for types B_l (l >= 2), E6, 2E6 and E7, leaving only types D and 2D open (abstract).
events.delivers: Verifies more families of simple groups for the inductive McKay condition; a step in the reduction, not a case of the McKay statement. Per the abstract, types D and 2D remain.
events.remains: The McKay conjecture as a whole; the inductive condition for types D and 2D.
events.direction: Partial verification of a reduction condition; does not decide McKay.

events.what_happened: Britta Späth, 'Extensions of characters in type D and the inductive McKay condition, I' (arXiv:2109.08230, 16 Sep 2021; published Cambridge online 8 Sep 2023 per search). Its abstract says it focuses on the last open case of groups of Lie type D and 2D and treats the A'(infinity) property.
events.delivers: Work on the last open family (types D and 2D) of the inductive McKay condition, per the abstract. I read only the abstract, so exactly what it verifies beyond that is not recorded.
events.remains: The inductive condition for types D and 2D in full (addressed by Part II and by the 2024 proof); McKay as a whole.
events.direction: Partial progress on a reduction condition; does not decide McKay.

events.what_happened: Britta Späth, 'Extensions of characters in type D and the inductive McKay condition, II' (arXiv:2304.07373, first posted 14 Apr 2023; v2 23 Sep 2025), published in Invent. Math. 242 (2025), 45-122. The v2 abstract says 'Theorem C establishes the McKay conjecture for the prime 3'.
events.revisions: v1 14 Apr 2023; v2 23 Sep 2025 (corrections and improvements suggested by referees). Invent. Math. 242 (2025), 45-122, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01354-9 (from search; not opened). I did not confirm that v1 already contained Theorem C; if it did not, the date for the prime-3 claim is 2025-09-23.
events.delivers: A restricted case: McKay for the prime 3 (Theorem C, per the v2 abstract). The paper also gives an Aut(G)-equivariant Jordan decomposition for quasisimple groups of Lie type and the A(infinity) property with extendibility.
events.remains: McKay for all primes other than 3. This was overtaken by the 2024 proof for all primes.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in Invent. Math. 242 (2025). The arXiv v2 says it includes corrections suggested by referees.

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for p = 3.

events.what_happened: Damiano Rossi, 'The McKay Conjecture and central isomorphic character triples' (arXiv:2204.10300, 21 Apr 2022; J. Algebra 618 (2023), 42-55 per search, not opened). It refines the IMN reduction: assuming the inductive McKay condition, it obtains a strong version of McKay that gives central isomorphic character triples (Conjecture A).
events.delivers: A conditional refinement: under the inductive McKay condition, a strong version of McKay with central isomorphic character triples. It does not prove McKay and is not McKay's statement.
events.remains: The McKay conjecture as stated, unconditionally.
events.direction: Refinement; neither confirms nor refutes the stated conjecture.

events.what_happened: Lucas Ruhstorfer and A. A. Schaeffer Fry, 'The McKay-Navarro conjecture for the prime 2' (arXiv:2211.14237, 25 Nov 2022; Adv. Math. 477 (2025), art. 110369, per a repository record, not opened).
events.delivers: Completes the McKay-Navarro (Galois-McKay) conjecture for the prime 2 by finishing the inductive McKay-Navarro conditions of Navarro-Späth-Vallejo. This is a Galois refinement, a different and stronger statement, and it covers one prime only.
events.remains: McKay-Navarro for odd primes. Nothing about McKay's conjecture itself is settled here.
events.direction: A stronger Galois form, confirmed at p = 2; it does not change the McKay statement.

events.what_happened: Lucas Ruhstorfer, 'The Alperin-McKay conjecture for the prime 2' (arXiv:2204.06373, 13 Apr 2022). Published as 'The Alperin-McKay and Brauer's height zero conjecture for the prime 2', Annals of Mathematics 201(2) (2025), 379-457 (received 14 Apr 2022, accepted 13 Mar 2024, published online 12 Mar 2025 per the Annals page).
events.delivers: Completes the Alperin-McKay conjecture and Brauer's height zero conjecture for the prime 2. This is a different, block-theoretic conjecture with the same family name; it does not touch the character-count statement of McKay's conjecture.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published after refereeing (Annals page opened; the page does not mention McKay outside Alperin-McKay).

events.direction: Different conjecture (Alperin-McKay, p = 2); no bearing on the McKay character count.

events.what_happened: Nguyen N. Hung, J. Miquel Martínez and Gabriel Navarro, 'Sum of the squares of the p'-character degrees' (arXiv:2505.21267, 27 May 2025). It studies the sum of squares of p'-degree irreducible character degrees in G and in N_G(P), and proves Giannelli's conjecture for p = 2 and some other cases. Published Pacific J. Math. 342 (2026), 351-380.
events.revisions: v1 27 May 2025; v3 9 Mar 2026 (arXiv). Pacific J. Math. 342 (2026), 351-380.
events.delivers: A quantity related to the McKay count (sum of squares of p'-degrees) and a refinement (Giannelli's conjecture) proved for p = 2 and some other cases. The abstract page does not mention the McKay conjecture; this is a different question.
events.remains: Nothing of McKay's statement is addressed.
events.direction: Partial results on a related refinement; no bearing on McKay's statement.

events.what_happened: Lucas Ruhstorfer, A. A. Schaeffer Fry, Britta Späth and Jay Taylor, 'Towards the inductive McKay-Navarro condition for groups of Lie type' (arXiv:2506.17123, 20 Jun 2025). Gathers tools for the inductive McKay-Navarro (Galois-McKay) condition for Lie-type groups and odd primes; gives a bijection for quasisimple groups of Lie type A; proves the conditions for unipotent characters.
events.delivers: Partial progress on a Galois refinement (McKay-Navarro) for Lie-type groups at odd primes. The abstract does not state the status of McKay's own conjecture.
events.remains: The inductive McKay-Navarro condition for most Lie-type groups at odd primes, and McKay-Navarro itself.
events.direction: Partial progress on a refinement; does not touch McKay's status as stated in its abstract.

events.what_happened: Eugenio Giannelli, 'McKay bijections and character degrees' (arXiv:2507.01730, first posted 2 Jul 2025). Proposes a refinement of McKay (Conjecture A: a bijection between p'-degree characters of G and N_G(P) with degree inequalities) and proves it for symmetric groups. Published Advances in Mathematics 498 (2026), 111029, accepted 14 May 2026 (Elsevier record via search; not opened). Its introduction treats McKay as settled: the conjecture 'was ultimately confirmed in full generality in [CS24] in 2024', and the bibliography entry CS24 is M. Cabanes and B. Späth, arXiv:2410.20392.
events.revisions: v1 2 Jul 2025; v2 3 Jul 2025; v3 14 May 2026 (arXiv).
events.delivers: A refinement that is strictly stronger than McKay (it asks for a degree-compatible bijection), proved for symmetric groups. It settles nothing about McKay's statement for the bullet; it treats McKay as already proved.
events.remains: The refinement for all finite groups; the bullet's statement is not addressed by this paper beyond citing CS24.
events.direction: Refinement; it cites the Cabanes-Späth proof as the confirmation of McKay.

events.what_happened: Lucas Ruhstorfer and A. A. Schaeffer Fry, 'The Isaacs-Navarro Galois conjecture' (arXiv:2509.02300, 2 Sep 2025). Proves the original Galois refinement of McKay (Isaacs-Navarro, 2002), which the authors describe as an important subcase of McKay-Navarro.
events.delivers: A Galois refinement of McKay, not McKay itself; a subcase of McKay-Navarro. It settles nothing for the bullet by itself.
events.remains: McKay's statement is not the subject; the broader McKay-Navarro conjecture remains as the authors describe it.
events.direction: Refinement (Galois); no direct bearing on McKay's statement.

events.what_happened: Adele Maltempo and Carolina Vallejo, 'The McKay conjecture with coprime group automorphisms and the Okuyama-Wajima argument' (arXiv:2512.13406, first posted 15 Dec 2025; v2 31 Jul 2026). The v1 abstract gives an A-equivariant McKay bijection for groups stabilising a Sylow p-subgroup, generalising a result of Gallagher and treating a p-solvable case that it says follows from Rossi. The journal version is listed as Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 230 (2026), art. 108155, received 12 Sep 2025, online 5 Dec 2025 (search listing; the publisher page did not load).
events.revisions: v1 15 Dec 2025; v2 31 Jul 2026. The v2 arXiv comment reads: 'Version 2 corrects an error in the statement of Theorem B that affected the proof, but not the statement, of Theorem A.' It also says 'The order of these results has now been swapped: the original Theorem B (now Theorem A) has been modified with a stronger hypothesis.' and 'The journal version of this paper in J. Pure Appl. Algebra has been retracted'.
events.delivers: A variant of McKay with extra automorphism equivariance and coprime hypotheses, with the p-solvable case as a consequence. It is not McKay's conjecture in general and is not stated for all groups.
events.remains: The statement of the bullet in full generality; this paper addresses a different (equivariant, coprime-automorphism) question.
events.doubts: The authors' own v2 changes the statement of Theorem B because of an error and reorders the theorems with a stronger hypothesis (arXiv comments, quoted in events). The same comment reports the journal version as retracted. A search listing shows the JPAA article published with no notice, and the publisher page did not load, so the retraction status is unresolved.

withdrawn.what: arXiv v2 comment: 'The journal version of this paper in J. Pure Appl. Algebra has been retracted.' No retraction notice was found on the publisher page (not readable).
withdrawn.date: Not stated; the comment sits in v2 dated 31 Jul 2026

events.direction: A variant result on a different (equivariant) question; no bearing on the stated conjecture beyond that.

events.what_happened: Izan Gómez-Taberner, 'On the inductive Giannelli-McKay condition for sporadic groups' (arXiv:2609.27042, 22 Sep 2026). It presents a computational framework (a GAP implementation is mentioned) for verifying Giannelli's refinement of McKay for sporadic simple groups and their universal covers, with theoretical reductions that bound the outer action.
events.delivers: Computational and theoretical reductions toward a refinement for sporadic groups. The abstract does not state a completed verification outcome. It is a refinement, not McKay's statement.
events.remains: The refinement for the remaining groups; McKay's statement is not addressed.
events.direction: Refinement for sporadic groups; no bearing on McKay's statement.

events.what_happened: Damiano Rossi, 'The Isaacs-Navarro-Wolf conjecture' (arXiv:2608.24685, 25 Aug 2026). A neighbouring problem (non-vanishing characters of solvable groups, not McKay). The abstract says it presents a proof 'discovered with the use of artificial intelligence systems'; the comments field says 'Artificial intelligence systems were used for this project'.
events.delivers: Nothing for the McKay bullet: it concerns the Isaacs-Navarro-Wolf conjecture on solvable groups. Recorded because the author is also the author of the 2022 refinement of the McKay reduction.
events.direction: Different conjecture; no bearing on McKay's statement.

events.what_happened: A Lean 4 / Mathlib statement of the Cabanes-Späth theorem (theorem_1_1: for a prime l and a Sylow l-subgroup S of a finite group X, the cardinality of McKayConjecture.Irr' X equals that of Irr' (normalizer S)) is held in the Imperial College London AnnalsChallenge repository (v1.0.0, file AnnalsChallenge/AnnalsOfMathematics/2026-203-3-McKayConjecture.lean) and on the lean-eval problem page. The repository says the proofs 'are left as sorry'. The problem page says the theorem declaration uses sorry, lists the informal solution as 'Unavailable', and shows the leaderboard as 'Loading'. Its 'All goals completed!' message refers to the statement compiling, not to a proof.
events.revisions: Repository: one commit, no date shown. Problem page: no date shown.
events.delivers: Nothing mathematical: a formal statement only, with no proof. It is a benchmark item for automated provers, which is why it is recorded.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as these pages show.
events.direction: A formal statement of the McKay equality; no proof, so no direction of settlement.

disputes.summary: Maltempo and Vallejo's arXiv v2 comment (31 Jul 2026) says the JPAA version of arXiv:2512.13406 has been retracted; a search listing shows JPAA 230 (2026), art. 108155 with no retraction notice; the publisher page did not load. This concerns a McKay variant, not the Cabanes-Späth proof, and I did not resolve it.

summary: Cabanes and Späth's 'The McKay Conjecture on character degrees' (arXiv:2410.20392, v1 27 Oct 2024, v2 1 May 2025; Annals of Mathematics 203(3) (2026), pp. 933-1032, accepted 17 Apr 2025 per the Annals page) claims the whole conjecture for every finite group and every prime. It reduces, via the Isaacs-Malle-Navarro (2007) reduction, to the inductive McKay condition for finite simple groups, then verifies that condition with the classification of finite simple groups, the main new work being in type D. I read the arXiv HTML rendering in two chunks (the PDF returned binary) and found no mention of computers, software, or AI; the Annals page, the Quanta article and Wikipedia are silent on AI too, so ai.none_found is true, with the caveat that the Späth ICMS talk PDF could not be read. The date is 27 Oct 2024, not 2023: Wikipedia's lead says 'In 2023, a proof of the general conjecture was announced', and Quanta says the announcement came in October 2023 to more than 100 mathematicians, but section 5.1 dates the first public written argument, and Wikipedia says the manuscript was available later in 2024; no earlier written version was found. The one close call is this date: a reader who counts the 2023 announcement would place the result before the window, and that reading is set out under competing_reading. Checking is thin. The only qualified check on record is Annals refereeing (reports not public), and the public comments in Quanta from Kessar, Navarro and Schaeffer Fry are praise, not stated verification. Searches of zbMATH, MathSciNet, MathOverflow and Tao's blog found no review, thread or post (these were search-only checks). No erratum or refutation turned up. Later work treats the result as settled: Giannelli (arXiv:2507.01730 v3; Adv. Math. 2026) cites CS24, whose bibliography entry is Cabanes and Späth arXiv:2410.20392, as the full proof, and builds a refinement on it; Hung-Martínez-Navarro (May 2025) and Ruhstorfer-Schaeffer Fry-Späth-Taylor (June 2025) do not state McKay's status in their abstracts. Earlier partial results are recorded as events: the 2007 reduction; Malle-Späth (p = 2, 2015; Annals 2016); Späth (p = 3, 2023; Invent. Math. 2025, dated to v1 but unconfirmed that v1 has Theorem C); and Cabanes-Späth's inductive-condition papers for types C (2016), B/E (2019), with Späth's type D part I (2021). Adjacent refinements and related conjectures are recorded with discounted scope: Ruhstorfer-Schaeffer Fry on McKay-Navarro at p = 2 (2022), Ruhstorfer on Alperin-McKay at p = 2 (2022), Rossi's refinement (2022), Ruhstorfer-Schaeffer Fry on the Isaacs-Navarro Galois conjecture (Sept 2025), Giannelli's symmetric-group refinement (July 2025), Gómez-Taberner's sporadic-group refinement (Sept 2026; AI used only for code, per its declaration) and Maltempo-Vallejo (Dec 2025; the disputed retraction is recorded under disputes). Rossi's AI-discovered proof of the Isaacs-Navarro-Wolf conjecture (Aug 2026) is a neighbouring problem with unnamed AI systems and does not bear on this bullet. The Imperial AnnalsChallenge repository and the lean-eval problem page carry only a Lean statement with sorry; the lean-eval leaderboard is dynamic and was not captured, so an AI prover solution cannot be ruled out. Dead ends: a 2026 arXiv paper on 'supernatural' primes (2608.08643) and a 2026 GPT counterexample paper (2608.29595) are unrelated; third-party review sites labelling Giannelli's paper 'AI First' describe their own tooling, and I did not rely on them.
competing_reading: Counting from the October 2023 announcement (Wikipedia: 'In 2023, a proof of the general conjecture was announced'; Quanta: announced in October 2023 to over 100 mathematicians), the result was public before 26 January 2024 and would be a pre-window event, not progress since the window opened. Against that, section 5.1 dates the first public written argument, and the earliest written version I can find is the arXiv posting of 27 Oct 2024; Annals received the paper on 31 Jul 2024. A separate, weaker reading: the Lean statement on lean-eval, with its 'All goals completed!' message, could be read as a formal verification, but the page's own note says the theorem declaration uses sorry, so I do not count it.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Any written manuscript circulated in 2023 (the October 2023 talks' slides or handouts, if they exist in dated form), which would move the first written argument out of the window. (b) The Annals referee reports or any published erratum (none found as of 13 Oct 2026). (c) A zbMATH or MathSciNet review, or an expert digest or Lean formalisation of the proof. (d) The lean-eval leaderboard entry for the Annals McKay problem, which would show whether any AI prover has submitted a machine-checked proof. (e) The publisher's status for Maltempo-Vallejo's JPAA article (not this paper), which would resolve the retraction dispute.

event.what_happened: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth, 'The McKay Conjecture on character degrees' (arXiv:2410.20392), claims a full proof: for every prime l and every finite group, the number of irreducible complex characters of degree prime to l equals that of the normalizer of a Sylow l-subgroup (the paper's Theorem A, labelled (MK)). The proof uses the Isaacs-Malle-Navarro (2007) reduction to the inductive McKay condition for finite simple groups, then verifies that condition using the classification of finite simple groups; the main technical work concerns characters of normalizers of Sylow d-tori (d >= 3) in simply connected groups of type D_l. The result was announced to audiences from October 2023 (Quanta says to more than 100 mathematicians; Wikipedia says 'in various conferences'), but the first public written argument is the arXiv v1 posted 27 Oct 2024. It was received by Annals of Mathematics on 31 Jul 2024, revised 13 Apr 2025, accepted 17 Apr 2025, and published in Annals 203(3), 2026, pp. 933-1032.
event.revisions: arXiv v1 27 Oct 2024; v2 1 May 2025 (current arXiv version). Journal: Annals of Mathematics 203(3), 2026, pp. 933-1032; received 2024-07-31, revised 2025-04-13, accepted 2025-04-17 (Annals page; the page gives no publication day). The Oct 2023 talks are not dated here: per section 5.1 the first written argument is the arXiv posting.
event.delivers: Settles the whole conjecture as stated: for every finite group X and every prime l, |Irr_l'(X)| = |Irr_l'(N_X(S))| for a Sylow l-subgroup S (arXiv HTML, Theorem A). The paper states the result without restriction to a class of groups or to particular primes. Its proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups, which the abstract names as an input.
event.remains: None of problem_asks is left open by the paper's own statements. The only wording gap is the one noted in problem_asks (the normalizer count's p'-restriction is implicit in the Wikipedia text and explicit in the paper).

judgement.why: Cabanes-Späth proves the statement for every finite group and every prime (Theorem A), which is the whole question; its first written argument is the 27 Oct 2024 arXiv posting (Annals received it 31 Jul 2024, also after the snapshot), so the Oct 2023 talks do not move it before 26 Jan 2024. Annals of Mathematics, a journal of record, accepted it after refereeing, which is digestion; the Quanta comments are only praise. No AI is credited. The earlier p = 2 and p = 3 results are cases, digested by Annals/Inventiones, and fall before the snapshot. The IMN reduction and the simple-group inductive-condition papers are steps toward a proof, not cases of the statement, so they score none. The Galois, Alperin-McKay, sum-of-squares, bijection, equivariant and sporadic refinements are variants. Rossi 2026 used AI on a different conjecture and its systems list is empty, so it scores none and earns nothing for this problem. The Lean item is a statement with sorry and no date.
judgement.doubts: The record does not confirm that Späth Part II v1 (Apr 2023) already contained Theorem C (p = 3); if it did not, that case dates to Sep 2025. Either way, the full proof outranks it. The lean-eval leaderboard was not captured, so the record cannot rule out a later AI-produced Lean proof.
